title: First: what is AI?
kit: Block 1 · the word
First: what is AI?
Artificial intelligence (AI)
Computer systems that do tasks which usually need a person's judgment: they recognize, predict, sort or create.
Normal software follows rules a person wrote…
…AI learns patterns from examples.
AI is a big family of tools, and Copilot is one member of it.

title: AI you used before Copilot.
kit: Block 1 · AI you already use
AI you used before Copilot.
These tools sort, recognize and predict. None of them writes you a letter.
Email: the spam filter decides which messages are junk.
Phone: face unlock recognizes your face.
Maps: the app predicts traffic and your arrival time.
Bank: an alert flags an unusual card payment as possible fraud.

title: So where do ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot fit?
kit: Block 1 · where LLMs fit
So where do ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot fit?
Every LLM is AI. Not every AI is an LLM.
Artificial intelligence
The whole family
Spam filters, face unlock, maps, fraud alerts, and everything below.
Machine learning
AI that learns from data
Most AI today: it finds patterns in examples.
Large language models
Machine learning on text
It learned from huge amounts of text, so it can write. ChatGPT, Claude, Gemini, and the models inside Copilot.

title: LLM: Large Language Model.
kit: Block 1 · the name
LLM: Large Language Model.
LLM
Large: it learned from a huge amount of text. Language: it works with words. Model: a program that learned patterns from examples.
A spam filter sorts the email you have…
…an LLM writes new text, one word at a time.
Each kind of AI makes its own kind of mistake, so each needs its own check.

title: Your phone keyboard guesses your next word.
kit: Block 1 · the picture
Your phone keyboard guesses your next word.
Copilot does the same thing with a much bigger memory. Its guesses sound right because it learned from a huge amount of text.

title: What Copilot really does.
kit: Block 1 · the idea
What Copilot really does.
Next-word prediction
Copilot writes by predicting the next word, one word at a time, from patterns in the text it learned from.
Like your phone keyboard…
…it picks a likely next word. Numbers and dates are words too.
It predicts. Without the source, it guesses or searches the web, and nothing checks it against Mutla's policy.

title: It writes by guessing the next word.
kit: Block 1 · live widget
It writes by guessing the next word.
At each step, every possible next word gets a score. The model picks one and repeats.
It predicts likely words. Mutla's policy says 15, but 30 is more common.

title: Fluent and wrong.
kit: Block 1 · the risk

title: Fluent, wrong, and sent.
kit: Block 1 · it happened for real
Fluent, wrong, and sent.
In each case, a person sent it without checking the source.
Sources: Mata v. Avianca, US District Court, New York, 22 June 2023 · Moffatt v. Air Canada, 2024 BCCRT 149 · Associated Press, 7 October 2025
New York court · 2023
Lawyers fined $5,000
Two lawyers filed a court brief with six cases that ChatGPT made up. They had asked ChatGPT if the cases were real, and it said yes. The judge fined them and their firm.
Air Canada · 2024
A chatbot invented a refund rule
The website chatbot told a passenger he could claim a bereavement discount after his flight. The real policy said before. A tribunal made the airline pay.
Deloitte Australia · 2025
Part of the fee paid back
A A$440,000 report for a government department had made-up references and a made-up quote from a court judgment. The firm refunded part of the fee.

Part
It tells Copilot
Example
